history.dynasty: Sikh (Guru Gobind Singh period; present structure 20th century)
history.period: Fort foundation 31 March 1689; present building completed 1970
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — Sikh gurdwara, keep-or-drop decision needed. Gurdwara Qila Anandgarh Sahib (Anandgarh Qila, 'fort of bliss') was one of the defensive forts built by Guru Gobind Singh around Anandpur Sahib; construction of the fort ring began in 1689 and took over ten years. Anandgarh was the Guru's headquarters - he is said to have spent about 16 years here - and the main store of Sikh arms and ammunition; it was the strongest of the forts and was never taken, only being occupied and demolished by the hill army on 6-7 December 1705 after the Guru left Anandpur. The site, about 800 metres south-east of Takht Sri Kesgarh Sahib, has a sacred Baoli Sahib (stepped well, 135 marbled steps). The present marble complex was raised in the 1970s by Sant Seva Singh (d. 1982) and his successors; an earlier fort-like building from the 1930s (Kartar Singh Kalasvalia) still stands on the hillock. name: Gurdwara Qila Anandgarh Sahib
town_description: Anandpur Sahib, in Rupnagar district at the Shivalik foothills, is one of Sikhism's holiest cities - the 'City of Bliss' founded by Guru Tegh Bahadur and the birthplace of the Khalsa. Its historic fort-gurdwara complex, the Virasat-e-Khalsa museum, and the annual Hola Mohalla gathering draw devotees worldwide.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International Airport, about 80 km away (~90 minutes by taxi); Amritsar's Sri Guru Ram Das Ji International Airport is about 170 km away.
travel.railway: Anandpur Sahib has its own railway station, connected to major cities.
travel.road: On the Guru Gobind Singh Marg (NH 205); well connected by bus/taxi from Chandigarh, Amritsar and Delhi.

visitor_information.best_time: March, during Hola Mohalla, the fort-town's great festival; October to March otherwise for pleasant weather.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Specific hours unverified; gurdwaras here are typically open from early morning (around 4:00 AM) to late evening (around 10:00 PM) - verify locally.
